newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: UN refugee chiefs see no exodus from Afghanistan.
newsitem.headline: UN refugee chiefs see no exodus from Afghanistan.

text.p: The United Nations refugee agency on Monday played down fears that recent territorial gains by the Islamic Taleban militia in northern Afghanistan might trigger an exodus of refugees to former Soviet republics in Central Asia.

"As far as I know...there is no fierce fighting in the north and so far there is no sign of a large movement of refugees from Afghanistan," Sadako Ogata, U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees, told a news conference in the Kazakh capital, Almaty.

Last weekend, the purist Islamic militia seized parts of northern Afghanistan from the opposition alliance, sending a wave of panic through ex-Soviet neighbours Tajikistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan and causing concern in Moscow.
The Central Asian states have expressed concern over both a possible advent of militant, Taleban-style Islam and a huge influx of refugees from Afghanistan.

Last month Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov said he feared that up to a million Afghan refugees could flood his impoverished and war-damaged country of 5.7 million in the event of fierce fighting across the frontier in Afghanistan.
Ogata, who on Sunday started a 10-day tour of the Central Asian states, said: "I hope that his (Rakhmonov's) prediction will not come true."

"There are still around 18,000 Tajik refugees in Afghanistan but whether the fighting will result in their movement, we will see," she added. Around 60,000 Tajiks fled to Afghanistan during the four-year civil war in Tajikistan, which ended last year.
Rupert Colville, regional public information officer for the refugee agency, said U.N. checkpoints in northern Afghanistan had so far witnessed no big movements of refugees.
"Right now there seems to be, thank goodness, not too much fighting going on in northern Afghanistan, and if that continues there may not be much displacement," he said.
An agency statement said the number of refugees from Afghanistan after years of instability is nearly 2.68 million, with 1.20 million living in Pakistan and 1.40 million in Iran.
Colville said that around 300,000 Afghans had been displaced inside Afghanistan since last October, when the Taleban launched an offensive northward from the capital, Kabul.
